tasks.short: Maintain correspondence files, activity records and follow-up status.

steps.what: Find correspondence and its case reference in the {HELPDESK} and {EMAIL}.
Save correspondence and attachments under the case reference in the {DOCS}.
Copy dates, recipients and reply status into the correspondence register in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Reconcile the register with case histories and correct missing or inconsistent entries.
Send overdue-reply and missing-record reminders through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure the {HELPDESK} to retain correspondence events and use a deterministic connector to file attachments in the {DOCS} with stable case references. Remove the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register, expose missing-event checks in the {HELPDESK}, and send deadline reminders through the {EMAIL}. A clerk approves corrections when records disagree.
tasks.previous_blocker: Messages, files and case status sit in separate places. Copying between them was easier to introduce than reliable matching, duplicate prevention and access controls.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case-event features can replace much of the register. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building the small connector and reconciliation checks; no model is needed at runtime.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy folders, shared case references and inconsistent permissions make migration costly. Retention, deletion and access must follow GDPR and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparently complete record conceals an unresolved promise or a misleading case history.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of correspondence approaching its reply deadline.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying activity entries to resolving missing records and overdue replies. The clerk can recommend queue priorities; formal decision rights do not change automatically.

reach.learn: Case ageing, service deadlines and how to distinguish missing records from genuinely unfinished work.

evidence.claim: The current steps, time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
TOPdesk Robin demonstrates structured, pre-filled request creation; it does not establish this filing design's savings.
Stable identifiers, event logging and deterministic reconciliation can replace duplicate activity registers.

assumptions: A representative team uses the {HELPDESK} for cases, the {DOCS} for files and a small duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register.
Correspondence usually carries a case reference; unmatched items enter an exception queue.
The design tracks case deadlines rather than scoring employee performance.
Build ranges cover one queue, access setup and any applicable employee consultation. Formal consultation can extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Whether a duplicate register exists or equivalent logging is already configured.
Available event interfaces, exports and document permissions.
Required retention periods and permitted corrections to historical records.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Can existing {HELPDESK} configuration replace the register without custom code?
Which event identifiers remain stable across replies, reopened cases and forwarded messages?
new_work: Resolve unmatched correspondence and disputed record corrections.
Monitor connector failures and duplicate-event checks.
Maintain filing, retention and reminder rules.

tasks.short: Read incoming correspondence, identify concerns and decide where each case should go.

steps.what: Open incoming correspondence in the {EMAIL} and find any existing case.
Read the message and attachments, then note the writer's concerns.

loop.input: Incoming correspondence, readable attachments and the linked case history.
loop.output: A concern summary with requested outcomes, issue labels, evidence quotations and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Require valid fields and source quotations. Treat attachments as data; reject unsupported summaries and flag conflicting requests.
loop.stop: One reading pass and one repair attempt within a fixed input limit. Unreadable, oversized or unresolved items go to the clerk with their originals.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text concerns and several requests in one letter cannot reliably be captured by fixed fields or keyword rules.

steps.what: Determine the case category, urgency and appropriate destination in the {HELPDESK}.
Assign the case owner and reply deadline in the {HELPDESK}.
Send a receipt notice through the {EMAIL}, stating the case reference and expected response.

tasks.design: Configure intake and duplicate linking in the {HELPDESK}, with a bounded reading loop producing a source-linked concern summary. Existing routing rules propose a destination for clerk approval, after which the {WORKFLOW} assigns ownership and sends an approved receipt template through the {EMAIL}. Substantive promises and case decisions stay outside the automatic receipt.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mail rules handle senders and keywords, but struggle with indirect concerns, attachments and several issues in one message.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded model call can turn varied text into structured notes. Existing queue rules then handle assignment and deadlines without autonomous investigation.
tasks.still_hard: Implicit urgency, legal notices, mixed languages and contradictory histories still require careful reading. Poor source material limits both summaries and human review.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the concern behind the stated request and recognising when normal routing would fail the writer.

ambition.what: A single coordinated response plan for letters containing several unrelated concerns.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time on ambiguous concerns and multi-team cases, with less opening, copying and acknowledgement work. Existing routing discretion remains; settlement and credit authority do not change.

reach.task: Clarify the outcome a customer actually wants.
reach.learn: Focused clarification questions, escalation signals and expectations across several service teams.

evidence.claim: The workflow, review shares and build ranges are estimates rather than observed results for this job.
TOPdesk Robin answers from a knowledge base or creates a pre-filled request, supporting structured handover feasibility.
Zendesk AI agents support customer questions through email and other channels, with integrations.

assumptions: Most intake is electronic; posted letters are already scanned before this task begins.
Reading produces a short case note, even where it is currently informal.
Routing approval is a brief clerk check; sensitive or unclear cases receive fuller review.
Receipt templates contain no remedy, liability admission or credit decision.
Build ranges include access and any applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Actual channel mix, attachment formats and languages.
Available routing rules, urgency definitions and legal-notice procedures.
How often one letter needs several case owners.
Whether existing {HELPDESK} features already provide adequate summaries.
Approved processing locations, model access and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: How often does a source-linked summary omit a second concern or an explicit deadline?
Which routing categories can existing configuration propose reliably?
Can duplicate linking avoid merging correspondence from different people sharing an address?
new_work: Read originals when summaries are uncertain, incomplete or rejected.
Review misroutes and maintain queue definitions.
Test summaries after policy, language or model changes.
Maintain receipt templates and service-calendar rules.

tasks.short: Gather relevant records, check their reliability and prepare suitable correspondence attachments.

steps.what: Find relevant customer, transaction and case records in the {CRM}, {ERP} and {HELPDESK}.
Collect invoices, delivery evidence and earlier correspondence from the {DOCS}.
Check evidence completeness, dates, amounts and consistency against the case.

loop.input: Retrieved records, an evidence checklist and exact-match results for references, dates and amounts.
loop.output: A source-linked discrepancy list, missing record list and unresolved factual conflicts.
loop.check: Code verifies identifiers and arithmetic. Every narrative discrepancy must cite source passages; the clerk resolves conflicts before evidence is marked checked.
loop.stop: One comparison pass and one repair attempt within a fixed document limit. Missing or conflicting evidence remains unresolved and goes to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Code handles structured fields, but delivery notes and earlier letters may describe events inconsistently in free text.

steps.what: Request missing transaction records from the finance team through the {EMAIL}.
Select, redact and attach records suitable for the intended recipient.

tasks.design: A deterministic service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieves records from the {CRM}, {ERP}, {HELPDESK} and {DOCS} using verified references and existing permissions. Code checks fields and builds the evidence pack; a bounded loop highlights narrative conflicts for clerk review, while the {WORKFLOW} requests missing records. A document generator applies approved disclosure rules, and the clerk approves the attachment pack before it reaches the sending step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different identifiers and permissions make gathering slow. Completeness also depends on descriptions spread across documents rather than a single checklist.
tasks.enabler_now: Small read-only connectors and document generators are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Bounded comparison can highlight textual conflicts without deciding which account is true.
tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence cannot be generated. Cross-customer identifiers, document versions and irreversible disclosure errors require careful controls and human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which evidence actually supports an explanation and what the recipient is entitled to receive.

ambition.what: A source-linked evidence explanation accompanying disputed-billing replies.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching folders to resolving factual conflicts and explaining evidence gaps. The clerk gains a stronger basis for challenging incomplete cases, with no automatic expansion of disclosure authority.

reach.task: Reconcile a disputed balance with invoices, payments and credits.
reach.learn: Transaction matching, the difference between a balance error and a service dispute, and escalation limits.

evidence.claim: The workflow, proposed evidence checks, time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Rossum checks document-derived order data against business rules and routes exceptions to people; this is an analogous validation pattern.
Zendesk supports retrieving order information through integrations, supporting linked case-data access.
Recipient-specific attachment approval and data minimisation are necessary design considerations under GDPR.

assumptions: Customer and transaction references allow exact matching for most cases.
The clerk already has legitimate access to the retrieved records; automation does not widen that access.
Missing finance evidence returns to the existing case and triggers the same completeness checks.
Automatic redaction covers defined fields; unusual disclosures require manual preparation.
Build ranges include scoped access and any applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Identifier quality and the frequency of records belonging to several customers.
Whether authorised interfaces or sufficiently current exports exist.
The authoritative source when records conflict.
Permitted recipients, redaction requirements and document retention periods.
The actual volume of missing evidence and unusual disclosure requests.
research_questions: What evidence checklist is sufficient for each correspondence category?
Can retrieval preserve source permissions and document-version references?
Which narrative discrepancies can reviewers verify quickly from quoted passages?
Can redaction be verified on the final exported attachment?
new_work: Resolve conflicting evidence and failed identity matches.
Follow up on missing records that remain unanswered.
Review attachment selection and unusual redactions.
Maintain connectors, evidence checklists and source mappings.

tasks.short: Prepare accurate correspondence about claims, credit, billing and service complaints.

steps.what: Choose the reply purpose, relevant policy and proposed remedy from the case.
Draft the reply, claim form or billing inquiry using templates in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Response brief, checked case evidence, approved policy passages and a selected template.
loop.output: Draft correspondence with source references for factual claims and placeholders for controlled transaction fields.
loop.check: Code checks required sections and protected wording. Unsupported facts, extra promises and changed remedy terms fail validation; the clerk reviews the final draft.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt within a fixed context limit. Failed validation returns a populated template and source pack for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard wording, but varied complaints need a coherent explanation tied to the writer's specific concerns.

steps.what: Insert verified account details, invoice lines and amounts from the {ERP}.
Review facts, tone, policy wording and attachments against the case evidence.
Approve exceptional remedies or commitments outside the clerk's delegated authority.
Approve release and send the correspondence with its attachments through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: An artefact generator combines approved templates from the {DOCS}, case evidence from the {HELPDESK} and exact transaction fields from the {ERP}; a bounded model loop drafts only the explanatory prose. The {WORKFLOW} routes exceptional commitments to a support supervisor and sends through the {EMAIL} after the clerk approves the recipient, final text and attachments. Sent correspondence becomes the input to the shared activity-record workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Template fields were easy to automate, but case-specific explanations still required substantial writing. Evidence, transaction details and approval history were scattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic assembly can handle fields, arithmetic and layout, while bounded drafting handles variable prose. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting these existing capabilities.
tasks.still_hard: Fair remedies, admissions of liability and explanations of disputed facts remain judgement calls. GDPR applies, including Article 22 where a solely automated decision has legal or similarly significant effects; drafting must not silently become a credit decision.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a fair response, making a difficult explanation credible and taking responsibility for promises made to the recipient.

ambition.what: Customers needing a plain-language explanation alongside formal billing or claim correspondence.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time composing standard passages and more time assessing remedies and explaining difficult outcomes. Existing remedy limits remain; wider settlement authority would require explicit delegation.

reach.task: Resolve a service complaint through an agreed remedy.
reach.learn: De-escalation, remedy options and how to confirm that the proposed outcome addresses the complaint.
Payment allocation, credit-note status and the boundary between correspondence and a credit decision.

evidence.claim: The workflow, remaining-time shares and build ranges are estimates for a scoped implementation.
Template assembly, exact field insertion and bounded drafting are feasible building blocks; the digest provides no correspondence-specific savings case.
The NBER support-assistant study reported 14% more issues resolved per hour overall; this does not establish the same gain for correspondence clerks.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its exceptions and safeguards.

assumptions: Supervisor approval is conditional; its time share is averaged across correspondence cases.
Routine cases skip supervisor approval under existing documented limits.
Invoice correspondence uses issued transaction records or clearly marked drafts; the generator does not post financial transactions.
The clerk's factual review and final release check are distinct: the latter confirms the actual recipient and final attachments.
The pilot starts with approved templates and one correspondence category.
Build ranges include access, policy review and any applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Actual correspondence mix, languages and approved templates.
Which remedies require supervisor, finance or legal approval.
Whether invoice preparation includes issuing or posting transactions.
Whether current policy supports a plain-language companion explanation.
Permitted model processing, retention and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which reply categories can use templates alone?
Can the generator keep amounts, policy clauses and approved remedies unchanged?
How often do reviewers find unsupported claims or incomplete explanations?
Can final release bind approval to the exact document version, recipient and attachments?
new_work: Review generated explanations against the evidence and requested outcome.
Handle rejected drafts and exceptional remedy approvals.
Maintain templates, policy versions and transaction-field mappings.
Sample sent correspondence for factual accuracy and clarity.
Monitor failed sends and prevent duplicate release.

role.altitude: The role shifts from finding, copying and formatting information toward resolving evidence conflicts, interpreting concerns and preparing fair explanations. Existing routing and remedy limits remain unless the employer explicitly delegates wider decisions.
reach: Customer service representatives: clarify desired outcomes and resolve complaints.
Credit clerks: reconcile disputed balances and explain transaction evidence.
First-line supervisors: prioritise overdue cases and coordinate multi-team replies.
skills_to_grow: Distinguish missing evidence from contradictory evidence.
Write clear explanations of difficult outcomes.
Apply disclosure rules and check final attachments.
Turn recurring exceptions into testable workflow rules.
Evaluate draft quality without trusting fluent wording.
role.ambitious_version: A correspondence specialist who coordinates complex written cases, builds evidence-backed explanations and proposes fair remedies within agreed authority, supported by shared records and controlled document generation.
